Less than a minute of the song is available.
More than a minute of the song is available.
A non-digital copy is available. Usually live performances or someone playing the song.
Only the instrumental of the song is available. Also could mean the vocals are different.
Full song is available, but with added tags not from the song itself.
Anything in-between Abysmal and High Quality. Noticeably worse than High Quality or CD Quality.
Full song that has been exported by anyone else who was not the intended person.
Anything greater than or equal to 128kbps (YouTube quality) and less than 320kbps.
The entire song is available, but not the original file.
Anything around 320kbps. Not a noticeable difference to Lossless quality.
The original entire file of a song is avaliable.
Raw audio data, usually from leaked stems or sessions. Useful for audio editing, but not noticeably different to CD Quality.
The version we have is only available through the vocals. This means the beat could be different.
Only really used for entries about unreleased albums. Useful for if we have certain portions of the album but not the entire thing.
The song is unavailable, but has been confirmed to exist by people who have worked with Kanye.
The song is unavailable, but has been said to exist by reputable people within the leak community. Please take with a grain of salt.

There have been reputable people who say the song does exist and reputable people who say the song doesn't exist. As it is not our place to say who's right or wrong, songs with conflicting sources will be marked as such.
Demo of an unreleased or throwaway track.
Stands for feature. Artist performs part of a song, finished and intended for release.
A track someone makes that isn't intended for themselves, but rather to be used as a reference for someone else

Stands for reference. Artist adds in unfinished parts of the song to fill in empty space or to be refactored in future versions of the track. Sometimes the ref artist does the full song (a ref track), but othertimes they just do a small part (ref feature) or even fills in parts of the song (punch-ins).
Original Version of a released or mostly finished track.
The song is made with other people, not as a feature but as a main artist. Usually reserved for songs with groups Kanye's apart of or for songs meant for collab albums.
A completed track that was never released.
Stands for performing. Used for groups like Wu-Tang Clan so we can specify which member performs on a leak or released song.
Unreleased song with [Artist] production, but no [Artist] vocals.
Producer is involved in creating/working on the beat, or mixing/mastering the audio.
Throwaway where [Artist] is just a feature.
We don't really know anything about what the person contributed, but we know they at least did something to the song.
Unreleased or unavailable remix by someone notable.
"Best Of", some of the best leaks hosted on the tracker.
We just don't know what it is. Usually only applies to Ref Tracks, Throwaways, and OGs.
"Grails", the most wanted songs that have not yet leaked in full.
Does not fit with any of the other types of leaks listed here.
"Wanted", Songs that are wanted, but not as wanted as "Grails".
Confirmed track for an unreleased album, this means it was not removed from the main sequence.
"Worst Of", some of the worst leaks hosted on the tracker.
A full copy of an unreleased album which likely has sequencing or transitions.
